rows.title: Policy divergence
rows.figure: Oct hold ~85%; ECB Dec 100%; BoC/BoE/RBNZ/BoJ live
rows.read: October is settled as a hold — Reuters' Friday wire put it at ~85%, up from ~70% Thursday night; December is now the debate. Correction: the ECB's Oct 29 meeting is NOT priced as a hike (Reuters Oct 16 bond report) — December is 100% with ≥1 more by April. Macklem leaned hawkish into Oct 28; the Nov 5 BoE hike case stands on the GDP beat; RBNZ Oct 28 is two-way; Ueda flagged overshoot risks into BoJ Oct 29-30. Blackout from Saturday.

rows.title: Growth differentials
rows.read: Two-way America: industrial production beat (+0.7% vs +0.4%, sixth straight gain — utilities +3.5%, manufacturing +0.3%, ex-autos +0.5%) while the NY Fed's October services index collapsed to -20.7 from -8.7 — factories up, services warning. UK GDP beat (+0.1% vs -0.1%, 2.1% y/y strongest since Aug 2022); NZ manufacturing PMI 56.5, strongest since 2021.

rows.title: Inflation
rows.read: Three hot prints in three days: CPI 3.7%, PPI +1.3% (6.3% y/y, biggest since Mar 2022), import prices +1.1% (+8.1% y/y, a four-year high — tariffs and energy feeding through). Eurozone CPI confirmed at 3.8% (three-year high, energy +18.9%). WTI back over $100 adds the energy kicker into every central bank's October/November meeting.

rows.title: Risk sentiment
rows.figure: AI-rout easing; DXY first weekly fall in 5
rows.read: Asia rebounded from Thursday's AI-led rout (Kospi +2.8%, Nikkei +1.8%) and Iran-escalation fears eased — the relief trade is the dollar fade: DXY -0.42% to 101.61, first weekly loss in five. But risk isn't gone: Hormuz flows run at 68% of baseline (Kpler), the Houthis hit Aden, and oil's back over $100 — the haven bid (CHF +1.4% in two sessions) is alive underneath.

rows.title: Terms of trade / commodities
rows.read: Ukraine's renewed refinery strikes sent Nov WTI +2.8% to $100.71 (first close over $100 in a month) and Dec Brent +3.2% to $109.28. The Brent-WTI spread near $10.7 is the geopolitical-premium gauge — wide. Vitol: Hormuz fuel-oil flows still down ≥800k tons/month vs February; Russian refinery hits add ~1M tons/month of fuel-oil loss. Caps: IEA's remaining 100M-barrel release, possible US shadow-fleet sanctions easing, Starshield pressure on Kyiv to stop the strikes.

rows.title: Positioning
rows.figure: DXY weekly fall; funds long AUD (79th pctile)
rows.read: First DXY weekly fall in five weeks after the long-dollar run. The contrarian flag stands: hedge funds are net LONG AUD at the 79th percentile — the squeeze thesis is broken; stretched longs mean the pain trade is down, not up. Dollar longs sit mid-range (54th pctile); euro shorts 44th, yen shorts 67th (less short than usual), franc shorts 41st, CAD shorts 31st — none crowded (CFTC TFF, report date Oct 6).

rows.title: Fiscal & sovereign risk
rows.read: The Treasury's books are official now: September's deficit was -$26.9B vs -$34.7B expected (narrower = better), but FY2026's $1.992T is the largest in five years (~6.2% of GDP) — tariff refunds ($145B after the SCOTUS ruling) ate into record customs duties, and debt service hit a record $1.36T. The 10-year at 5.113%: deficit news is a negative tint for Treasuries. France: OAT-Bund 135.2bp, Oct 20 revenue vote, Moody's Oct 23; the EU's €100B+ war-driven fossil import bill is the euro's winter drag.
